ARCS kitMolecule 65question-pair

Question Pair

Set what the reader said beside the question worth asking about it, one row a point, so every question visibly comes from their own words.

States

Anatomy

#PartType roleToken (CSS variable)
1FrameSurface card, hairline border, rows split by hairlines; two equal columns split by a hairlinesurface, border, ds-r-md
2Column headsMono, uppercase, label step, on a tinted bar; the answer column head in cyansurface-2, muted, cyan
3SaidTheir point, in their words, secondary texttext-secondary
4AskThe question, primary texttext

Usage

Use it when

  • Every question or recommendation traces to something the counterpart said, and showing that trace is the point.
  • A proposal or brief where the reader should recognise their own words before they read yours.

Do not use it when

  • Do not paraphrase the left column into your vocabulary; it is their words or it is not this part.
  • Do not use it for a two-column comparison of options; that is a table, not a question pair.

Data it reads

FieldTypeRequiredNote
heads[said, ask]yesColumn heads, for example What you raised and Worth asking.
rows[]{said, ask}yesOne row a point. Plain text.

Access

  • Column heads are h3 elements; each row reads said, then ask, in source order.
  • On a phone the ask carries a visible text lead, so the pairing never depends on colour or column position.
  • The grid uses minmax(0, 1fr), so large text wraps inside the cell.
